title: Methods perform actions
summary: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it.
introduction: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it.

blocks.code:
const book = { title: "Moon", describe() { return this.title + " book"; } };
console.log(book.describe());
blocks.title: Methods perform actions

blocks.text: The result is Moon book. The parentheses call the method.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the title and call describe again.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: An arrow function does not create its own this value. Use the method form shown here.
For more detail later, use this [Object-Oriented Programming further reading](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Advanced_JavaScript_objects).
